independence_statement: This is an independent image-only reading of scan027. I consulted only CONVENTIONS.md, the assigned scan027 boxes TSV, the assigned whole source JPG, and my own independently generated scan027 crops. I did not consult witnesses, first readings, page transcriptions, other readers' notes or comparison results, including the subsequent scan033 adjudication. I used no OCR, recognition library, external research, or TeX compilation. All 23 required box images were personally inspected.
crop_processing: Each required box was cropped directly from the whole JPG at its original coordinates, autocontrasted with cutoff 0.5, resized proportionally to width 3000 with Pillow LANCZOS, and modestly sharpened using UnsharpMask(radius=1.2, percent=110, threshold=3). All rotations were zero. No strokes were erased or synthesized. Supplementary details used the same process.
time_recording: Times are UTC results from clock__curr_time at the actual image-viewing calls. A supplementary batch whose output was truncated was not counted; those images were viewed again successfully and only the successful viewing times are recorded.

boxes.visual_observations: The first digit has a bowed upper stroke with a descending diagonal and low foot; the second has an ascending curved back and a small closed lower loop. These read 26. No terminal punctuation is visible. The numeral is centered above the text.

Long strokes cross the word and F, establishing cancellation; the first word remains uncertain because several letter joins are covered.

The first relation has two distinct left-facing angles. The second has an upper curved angle and separate lower curved stroke. The words relations, ordre, déterminent and mutuellement have continuous readable letter sequences. A dense comma-shaped mark follows de at the first line end, and it has been retained despite the unusual syntax.

Each less-than-or-equal sign has a distinct lower line. After Peut-on de there are two parallel horizontal strokes, transcribed literally as an equals sign rather than expanded. The following line has the full exprimer phrase and a terminal hooked question mark with its dot.
Two separate tall hooks stand in the left margin, each over a dark lower dot. Their spacing and complete hook-dot construction support two question marks rather than alphabetic letters.

The second-line initial word has a tall first t, reduced o/u strokes, a second t and an open final e. Its long upper horizontal joins the t crossbars; a separate lower horizontal is an underline, with no secure independent cancellation stroke. Contrée has a tall t and a small accent over the final portion. The following via la condition is on the same baseline.

The small addition above the baseline contains an upright/slanted not-equal-like mark and a closed oval, favored as zero but not securely distinguished from an empty-set form. A curved attachment line rises from the H/non area toward it. Non vide remains on the baseline with a distinct underline; the attachment line is not treated as a deletion.
A clear opening parenthesis precedes et. The t is high, si and on are compressed low groups, and avait ends with a visible i dot and t stroke. There is no closing parenthesis within the box.

The fragment has de followed by an open G, par with a descender, and C5. The 5 has a short upper bar and angular turn over its lower curve. A comma is visible at the right. No preceding unseen words are supplied.

After donc the on/est groups are compressed. The following word has low r-like onset, connected m/n arches, and a final accented e-like ending, supporting ramené but not at full confidence. Ceci is followed by a dark point. H, both left angles, and G at the right remain legible under a continuous crossing line, so that formula and its comma are enclosed as deleted.

The main formula has two left angles before G and a long double arrow toward H equals a slashed empty-set-shaped oval with a clearly lowered F. Below it an opening parenthesis and i.e. introduce a smaller addition. The abbreviation after H starts with a low c/o cluster and ends in a downward v-like hook and dot; no secure p descender can be separated, so conv. is preferred and comp. retained as an alternative. The addition continues à G et and H intersection G equals empty set. No closing parenthesis is visible.

The small interlinear phrase begins i.e. Its formula has leaning outer uprights around a G-like curl and prime on the left and two uprights plus H crossbar on the right. The possible equals lies where two long cancellation strokes pass, so the full bar formula is doubtful. Those near-parallel crossing strokes continue through the right expression and establish deletion of the interlinear phrase.

Disjoint appears in both lines; the first has a tall d and descending j, while the second is compressed but retains the same main strokes. The cancelled small i.e. formula is above the comparison. A smaller par C-number addition sits by the second G-prime with a curved leader. The ending H=empty set, OK, exclamation point and closing parenthesis are visible; no opening parenthesis is invented for this excerpt.

The following narrow upright is favored as 1; it overlaps the descending j from disjoint above, and a possible angular 4 cannot be excluded. A curved leader below links the addition with the G-prime line. It is an insertion, not a struck phrase.
